claim: Visitors can try a realistic, populated sample in one click.
sandbox: a fresh browser opens /demo/, sees the populated support handoff, changes cleanup mode, and observes changed output

claim: Demo sample changes are separate from real app and license data, and Reset demo restores the sample.
sandbox: a fresh context changes and resets the demo, leaves through Start for real, confirms demo data is discarded, and asserts real-data and license namespaces are untouched

claim: The demo works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: the test creates its own browser context, loads /demo/, waits for its service worker, goes offline, reloads, and observes the supplied sample

claim: The demo sends no data to another service.
sandbox: a fresh context records every request while changing the sample and asserts that every request is same-origin

claim: The desktop app loads a realistic sample project without saving it.
sandbox: the browser app entry loads its shipped sample project and asserts the usable populated output and unsaved status

claim: The app reads a selected image with bundled local OCR, copies the result, sends no capture to another origin, and discards capture pixels after use.
where: landing page, app privacy note, privacy page, README
sandbox: a generated screenshot is selected and recognized with bundled worker, core, and English data; requests stay same-origin; clipboard output matches; the blob URL is revoked

claim: Installed OCR works without an internet connection.
where: landing first-screen facts, app status, README
sandbox: the generated-image OCR flow blocks every non-app origin and still produces and copies the expected text with bundled files

claim: The app creates no capture history or telemetry during OCR.
where: landing page, app privacy note, privacy page, README
sandbox: the complete generated-image OCR and copy flow records every request, requires same-origin traffic, and confirms app localStorage remains empty

claim: Ctrl/Cmd Shift 2 starts the user-initiated capture flow.
where: landing how-it-works section, app first screen, README
sandbox: the desktop browser app entry receives Ctrl+Shift+2, opens its image chooser fallback, and announces that installed builds use the same capture shortcut

claim: The region selector works with Arrow keys, Shift plus Arrow keys, Enter, and Escape.
sandbox: a generated screenshot enters the selector; Arrow moves, Shift+Arrow resizes, Enter recognizes, and the recovery test covers Escape

claim: Cancel, too-small selections, and corrupt images recover without retaining capture pixels or trapping the user.
sandbox: the app cancels and revokes a valid blob, shows a visible small-selection error, then handles a corrupt PNG without a page error or stuck overlay

claim: Paragraph, code, table, and Markdown cleanup produce reusable text.
sandbox: recorded OCR-like fixtures assert dehyphenated paragraphs, repaired code quotes, tabular columns, and complete Markdown output

claim: English, Spanish, and German OCR language data is bundled at the disclosed sizes; Spanish and German require Pro.
sandbox: a cached valid fixture license selects Spanish and German, recognizes supplied words with both local models, records only same-origin requests, and measures each language file byte-for-byte

claim: Pro costs $12 once, gates specialist features, accepts a returned license, and provides a visible browser-to-app transfer path.
where: landing pricing, app license dialog, terms, README
sandbox: the test checks exact offer copy/link, returns a fixture token, strips it from the URL, copies it, proves free gating, verifies through a recorded valid API response, and selects a Pro feature

claim: The Linux one-line installer verifies SHA-256 and installs an executable command in a clean home.
sandbox: a temporary consumer home with no Downloads directory installs a local fixture AppImage through the real shell installer, compares bytes, checks executable mode, and runs it
